title: AWS access key ID alone: confidentiality not stated
summary: An AWS access key ID (AKIA..., 20 characters) appearing alone, with no secret access key anywhere in the input. Value is synthetic.
rationale: The IAM user guide describes the access key ID and the secret as two parts of an access key and warns against giving access keys to unauthorized parties, but no page read states whether the ID alone is confidential. Treating it as a secret and treating it as harmless are both unsupported, so the expectation is left open instead of inheriting the secret's outcome.

expectation.rationale: Unresolved: the pages read (IAM access keys guide, STS Credentials type) do not say whether an access key ID is confidential on its own. Would resolve: a provider statement classifying the access key ID, or a maintainer project-policy decision recorded with a second reviewer.

sources.supports: describes the ID as one of two parts; no statement on the ID's confidentiality alone
sources.locator: Manage access keys for IAM users, introduction

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
